correctness.rationale: The gradient deletion identity supplies one monic quadratic for all coordinates. Exact two-value difference and sum-of-squares identities force (m−1)a=(r−1)b=0, including zero/nonzero boundaries; the all-equal boundary gives n≡1 or2. Nullstellensatz proves the radical equalities. All linear component ideals are distinct and inclusion-incomparable. Hessian rank is n−1 along generic lines and n−2 along generic planes. Replayed finite-field tests show the same patterns but are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Xie (arXiv:2610.00259v1) covers the extremal n≡2 planes (explicitly not claimed as new), but expressly leaves smaller-dimensional components unclassified. The novel statement determines every line/minimal prime and exact degree in the complementary n≠2 regime. Orzel treats zero-and-gradient dimension and Cafure et al. give only partition containment. Published-finding and direct literature search found no explicit covering formula, though undiscovered equivalent formulations remain possible.

value.rationale: The irredundant classification fills a natural smaller-component gap named in the recent initiating paper for the first nontrivial elementary symmetric cubic. Exact radical ideals, component counts, degrees and generic smoothness across every odd prime and all n are structurally informative, rather than a single arbitrary sample. Even where dimension is always 1, the component count can grow combinatorially (n=6, p=3 gives 21 lines). No claim of a downstream breakthrough is required.
